extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, KIPO staff, patent applicants and patent attorneys practicing before the Korean Intellectual Property Office
extracted.subtask_short: KIPO document service and fee rules
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and standards governing service of documents (personal, mail, publication, electronic, special service) and the payment, refund, exemption, and calculation of patent-related fees under the Korean Patent Act and subordinate rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-day conduct when mixed filing media
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some filings are submitted online and the rest are submitted in an electronic recording medium or in writing, all of the concerned patent-related proceedings shall be conducted on the same day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents affecting gain or loss of patent right are subject to service
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents whose results affect the gain or loss of a patent right or the interest of a party in a patent-related proceeding are defined as documents subject to service under the Patent Act and subordinate statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Act and subordinate statutes also specify methods for service of such documents; documents not so defined may be prescribed by the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner-prescribed service for non-subject documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of documents other than those expressly subject to service under the Act shall be prescribed by the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIPO currently operates sending of such documents in the same way as documents subject to service (e.g., dispatch boxes, administrative practice regs, PatentNet).

rubrics_metrics.name: List of documents subject to service (examination-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents subject to service related to examination include a certified copy of the decision to grant a patent, a notification of invalidation under Article 16(2), and a certified copy of the decision under Article 214(3) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted methods of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of service include personal service, service by mail (registered mail), and service by publication, as prescribed in Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service by electronic information and communication network is also authorized where the recipient has notified use of electronic documents (see electronic service entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of electronic and written service (where permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of documents through an information and communication network has the same effect as service of written documents for persons who have notified use of electronic documents to KIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All documents can be served in electronic form except where special provisions in the Patent Act require otherwise (example: documents requiring special service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Government Electronic Document System for examiner notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examination result affects gain or change of a patent right but required notification format is not reflected in the patent examination processing system, an examiner shall notify the examination results by using the Government Electronic Document System (On-nara system).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal service receipt requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal service requires handing over documents to the party or their representative in person and obtaining a receipt stating the date of receipt and the name of the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation of a receipt may be replaced by stamping the registered seal on the document service registry and postage payment registry placed at the dispatch box; if the recipient is not a patent attorney, the patent attorney’s registered seal and a representative’s seal shall be stamped together (Article 7 of the Regulation for Administrative Practices of Dispatch Box).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered mail as default mail service
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of documents shall be conducted by registered mail, except where a party or representative receives documents in person or via an information and communication network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where documents are served by mail, the receipt of the registered mail issued by a post office shall be placed in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special service method for trial/retrial/revocation decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Written rulings or decisions on trial, retrial or revocation of a patent right must be served by the special service method prescribed by the Postal Service Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, an examiner may use the information and communication network when serving such ruling/decision to a person who filed documents in electronic form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient identity and order rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents must be served to the person to whom the documents are to be served (applicant or their representative). If there is a representative, the representative is the recipient; if a sub-agent or a new representative is appointed mid-proceeding, that sub-agent/representative shall be the recipient except for special reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there are multiple representatives, the representative first written in the application is the recipient unless special reasons; where there is a representative with general power and others, serve first to a representative with special power of attorney; where a person is incompetent, serve to legal representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service to common representative for joint proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more persons jointly conduct a patent-related proceeding and a common representative has been appointed, documents shall be served to the common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no common representative notification exists, the applicant first written in the documents shall receive such documents, except for special reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service to persons in prison/detention
rubrics_metrics.description: Any service to a person who is in prison or a detention house shall be made to the head of that prison or detention house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service to designated representative notified to Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a representative is designated to receive documents and that designation is notified to the Commissioner of KIPO (or president of IPTAB), any service of documents shall be made to the designated representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service at domicile or place of business; reporting changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents shall be served to the domicile or place of business of the person to be served; if the person has reported another place for receiving documents, serve there. Changes to the place to be served must be reported without delay to the Commissioner of KIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a person refuses to receive documents without justifiable reason making service impossible, service shall be considered made on the day of sending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication when domicile/place unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: If the domicile or place of business of the person to be served is unclear and cannot be confirmed even using the resident registration number sharing system, service shall be made by publication. If multiple persons are involved and domiciles of all cannot be identified, publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For juristic persons the resident registration number system cannot be used; examiners must attempt to serve at the statutory domicile at least once before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure before service by publication (investigation steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents are returned, the director enters dispatch number and grounds for return into the data system and notifies examination management; examiner must attempt to confirm domicile via administrative data sharing system and other means (calling phone number, other checks) prior to deciding on publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If domicile identified later, resend guidance for notification of change along with returned document to newly-identified domicile. Only if domicile cannot be identified after all attempts should service by public announcement be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court precedent on publication (must attempt address search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision to make service by publication without attempting to find the plaintiff's address by ex officio investigation (e.g., via other administrative institutions) is improper (Case No. 91 Hu 59, Supreme Court 8 Oct 1991).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should exhaust investigations using available administrative information before resorting to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and timing of service by publication
rubrics_metrics.description: When service by publication is first made, it becomes effective two weeks after disclosure in the patent gazette; subsequent service by publication to the same party takes effect on the following date of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the address changes after publication, documents shall be resent unless the proceeding has been terminated; statutory/designated periods are calculated from the effective date by publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to repeat publication vs. mail after initial publication
rubrics_metrics.description: After an initial service by publication, if the examiner intends to deliver relevant documents again but no notification of change was made despite notice and the ground for return was 'Recipient Absence', 'Moved' or 'Address Unknown', the examiner shall immediately make service by publication again rather than delivering by mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and attachments for publication when requested
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party requests the notification of documents to be publicly announced without changing address, the examiner shall deliver the documents by stating their contents or attaching the documents to be publicly announced at the announcement of the report on change of applicant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may do the same when the examiner recognizes such decisions are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returned-documents treatment applies when absent long or business closed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a party is absent from the submitted address for a long time or a business is temporarily shut down without change of domicile/place of business, the treatment applicable to returned documents shall apply mutatis mutandis to service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents that must/need not be served by publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents under Article 218 of the Patent Act and Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree must be served by publication. Other documents need not necessarily be served by publication if they have little influence on the right to obtain a patent and future notifications on such proceedings are possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a notification about the possibility of use of documents to an information provider may be skipped from publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple parties: re-serve returned documents before publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are more than two parties to be served (e.g., multiple applicants) and delivered documents are returned, the examiner shall serve the documents again to the other party rather than serve by publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents were delivered to a representative of more than two parties but returned, the examiner shall not directly deliver to the parties other than the representative because only the representative can conduct the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct-delivery request after publication: receipt storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a party requests direct delivery of documents after service by publication, a receipt for a written application shall be stored in the file wrapper. For electronically-filed applications, the examiner shall request the history of the written application from the Information Development Division and keep the receipt in each examination division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service to overseas residents with/without patent administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: For an overseas resident having a patent administrator, documents shall be served on the patent administrator. For an overseas resident without a patent administrator, documents may be sent by registered airmail and are deemed served on the mailing date (sending theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special service for adjudications, non-exclusive license rulings, revocations
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjudications or decisions on trial, review, ruling on establishment of non-exclusive license and revocation of patent right shall be delivered by the special service method prescribed by the Postal Service Act and its Enforcement Decree; similar special service applies to certain utility model proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the recipient has filed a report of using the electronic filing system, the information and communications network can be utilized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official fees payable by persons conducting patent-related proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who performs a patent-related proceeding (e.g., filing an application or a request for examination) shall pay official fees (Article 82). If the number of claims is increased by amendment after a third party filed a request for examination, the applicant shall pay fees for the increased claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods of payment and deadlines are prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and Fee Collection Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner authority to exempt/reduce fees (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of KIPO shall exempt payment of certain patent fees or official fees (e.g., applications/patents belonging to the State; official fees for petitions for invalidation action by examiner under specified Articles). The Commissioner may also reduce or exempt fees for persons eligible under the National Basic Living Security Act or others specified by Ordinance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking reduction/exemption must submit documents specified by Ordinance of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund conditions for patent and official fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees or official fees paid shall be refunded only in specified cases at the payer’s request, including: fees paid erroneously; portions of fees for years after final revocation/invalidating decisions; fees for filing/priority when application voluntarily withdrawn within one month (with exclusions); fees for examination request where application withdrawn before certain events; various half-refund rules for dismissed/withdrawn/rejected trial participation requests; and other enumerated situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim for refund may not be filed after three years from the date when the person receives notice of the applicable refund case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-related fees are the responsibility of the person conducting the proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent-related fees shall be paid by the person conducting the patent-related proceeding. If someone other than the applicant conducts the proceeding (e.g., files a request for trial, expedited examination), that person pays the relevant fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fees increase due to amendment after a request for examination is made, the applicant must pay additional fees for the newly-added claims; fees already paid are not refunded if claims are deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of official fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Types include application fees (patent, utility model, divisional, converted), priority claim fees, fees for request for examination (including reexamination and expedited examination), fee for change of applicant, amendment fees, and fees for extension of statutory/designated periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts and details are listed in the Fee Collection Rules and on KIPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and methods for fee payment and receipt numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents are submitted, the registration number of the documents shall be deemed the payer number. Fees shall be paid to a designated bank or post office by the following day of receipt of the documents. Fees can be paid via electronic payment (Internet Giro) or in cash with prescribed forms; postal money order required when paid by mail. Fees paid after the payment period shall be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional fees must be paid along with basic fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of unpaid fees for requests for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request for examination is made, the requesting person must pay the fees for request for examination. If such fees are unpaid, an examiner shall order amendment; if deficiencies are not addressed after amendment, the examiner may invalidate the request for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting claims for fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: In estimating fees for a request for examination, the number of claims shall be counted by each claim regardless of whether claims are independent or dependent; a dependent claim is counted as one even if dependent on more than two claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific counting rules for scenarios: (①) if request for examination filed at same time as filing or no amendment before request, count initial claims; (②) if amendments before request, count final claims after amendment; (③) if request and amendment submitted simultaneously, count claims at time of amendment submission; (④) if claims increased after request, additional fees are based on increased claims regardless of deleted claims. Examples provided in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of additional examination fees after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: After making a request for examination, where fees for the request are increased because of amendment (e.g., new claims added), the applicant shall pay the additional fees when submitting the written amendment. Deleted claims do not entitle the applicant to a refund of fees already paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: added five new claims after amendment -> additional fee based on newly-added 5 claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete exemption program (limited cases per year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain persons (categories listed) shall not pay application fees and fees of a request for examination for up to 10 cases per year for patent and utility model registrations, and shall not pay patent fees or fees for utility model registration for the first three years when they file or register rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment fees other than application and examination request fees are still collected. Each requirement for exemption must be met at time of document submission; if eligibility lapses by registration time, fee exemptions for the first three years will not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects and evidential documents for complete exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible subjects include: recipients of National Basic Livelihood Security Act benefits (when inventor and applicant identical), persons of national merit and surviving families, registered disabled persons, elementary/middle school students, persons aged >=6 and <19, persons in military service or public service. Evidential documents (e.g., copy of identification booklet for disabled, certificate of attendance, certificate of military service) must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is assessed at time of submission and references specific statutory definitions and articles for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial exemption eligibility and amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial exemption from payment of application fees, request for examination fees, patent fees for first three years, or utility model registration fees is granted to individuals, SMEs under the Framework Act on SMEs, joint research between conglomerates and SMEs, public research organizations, and technology transfer task forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only for individuals and SMEs and certain organizations, 30% of the patent fee and the utility model registration fee for years 4 to 9 is reduced; in calculating exemption amounts, amounts less than 100 won are not included. If applicant files personally and seeks exemption, the applicant must be the inventor or designer.
